Guy Kinnings, the DP World Tour’s Chief Executive, said: “Following the success of our 2026 season, in which three of our members won Major Championships and our players regularly showcased their talent on the global stage, our 2027 season is set to be one of the most keenly contested campaigns in our 55-year history.

“There has been significant change in the landscape of men’s professional golf over the past 12 months. As golf’s global Tour, we have taken a pragmatic approach to this unique and unprecedented situation as we go into next year, always with the best interests of our entire membership at the forefront of our minds.

“We realise there are different viewpoints but this approach, discussed and agreed with our Tournament Committee and allied to this responsibly managed programme of invites, will add value which, in turn, will benefit the Tour as a whole.

“We therefore look forward to beginning our 2027 season at the BMW Australian PGA Championship next week, a season where our fans will enjoy enhanced and competitive fields at our historic tournaments around the world.”

title: DP World Tour Play-Offs: Race to Dubai battle and PGA Tour dual member cards decided in compelling climax
article_text:
In a gripping climax to the DP World Tour season, the destiny of the 2026 Race to Dubai title went down to the final hole.

For a time during Sunday's final round at the DP World Tour Championship, just one-tenth of a point separated Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy as the pair battled for the Race to Dubai crown.

With Tyrrell Hatton playing his way to a commanding victory, all eyes were on who would claim the Harry Vardon Trophy as the Tour's best-performing player across the 42-event campaign.

At the end of a day that saw the overall lead in the Rankings chop and change with remarkable regularity, McIlroy celebrated drawing level with Colin Montgomerie on eight Race to Dubai titles as Chacarra fell just short despite a breakthrough campaign.

Ahead of the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, the penultimate event of the season, earlier this month, Chacarra entered the closing stretch as the man in pole position.

With three wins to his name, the Spaniard led from Patrick Reed and McIlroy in third as the main protagonists in the contest to be crowned European Number One.

Holding a lead of 669 points over Reed in second, and a cushion of just under 1,000 points above McIlroy in third, there were even scenarios where Chacarra could wrap up matters with a win at Yas Links.

But come the close of proceedings in Abu Dhabi, McIlroy had closed the gap by almost half to 533.93 points with a third-place finish.

Reed, by contrast, finished in a tie for 43rd and arrived for the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events requiring at worst to finish in a two-way tie for second to stand a chance of winning the Race to Dubai.

But after scores of 75 and 77 over the opening two rounds over the Earth course at Jumeirah Golf Estates, the American was out of the picture and it was all down to Chacarra and McIlroy over the weekend.

After the third round, things looked favourable for Chacarra as he and McIlroy - a repeat winner at the Masters Tournament in April - both sat in a tie for fourth at five under.

To add to the drama, McIlroy and Chacarra were separated by just one group on the final day, with the latter having to react at every step.

But Chacarra appeared unfazed, making four birdies across his opening eight holes, before a run of three bogeys around the turn halted his momentum. To his credit, he birdied the 13th and 14th and was back into the lead on the Rankings.

The telling moment came at the 16th, when McIlroy set up a birdie - his lone gain on the back nine - to move back ahead as the gutsy Chacarra could only par his closing three holes.

With that, and with Mikael Lindberg and then Victor Perez unable to match or better McIlroy's total of ten under for the week, the celebrations began.

"This is probably a good thing, but I wasn't aware of how much it was sort of going back and forth until the 16th," McIlroy later reflected of his closing bogey-free 67.

"When I was walking to the green, I saw that he was projected first. Then when I made my birdie and I'm walking off the green, I saw I was projected first. I was a little nervous going to the last couple of holes.

"I guess I did what I needed to do and I shot a good score today. A lot of other things went my way today, as well.

"No one made a run. Eugenio played pretty good but none of the chasing pack did anything... thankfully everything fell my way today."

Another intriguing subplot across the Play-Offs surrounded which players would have dual membership with the PGA Tour next season.

While for Chacarra and Reed it was all but a formality, along with other multiple winners across the campaign in South African pair Casey Jarvis and Jayden Schaper, others still had more substantial work to do.

Another player who appeared comfortable was Jacob Skov Olesen - a graduate of Qualifying School in 2024 - as he produced a run of consistent form, including a runner-up finish among two top tens across the Back 9.

Daniel Hillier was also feeling fairly comfortable aheading into the Play-Offs. On the bubble for much of the Back 9, a runner-up finish - a third of his campaign - at the DP World India Championship backed up by a top-15 finish at the Genesis Championship helped the New Zealander arrive in the UAE shorn of the stress he faced last year when he missed out by one spot.

The player to face the biggest case of heartbreak this time was Mikael Lindberg.

A breakthrough DP World Tour winner in Türkiye earlier in the season, the Swede was projected to finish among the top ten non exempt performers on the Race to Dubai Rankings for much of the final round in Dubai before a bogey-bogey finish dropped him outside the group of qualifying players.

His missed opportunity benefited Joe Dean, with the Englishman able to breathe a sigh of relief after a closing 74 had left his status in doubt.

For Bernd Wiesberger, a top-five finish in Abu Dhabi helped his cause no end, while fellow former Ryder Cupper Andy Sullivan closed out his season with back-to-back top-15 finishes to land him full status on the PGA Tour for the first time.

title: Chad Ramey is mistake-free in winning Tour’s Austin event. Thanks to a ‘motto’
article_text:
Like Blades Brown. He won last week on the PGA Tour. He’ll likely win a bunch more. He’s just 19, after all.

Then there was Austin Smotherman. He won his first PGA Tour event at the start of last month. Then he won again, two weeks later. Thrice in the fall would be nice.

And don’t forget about Max Homa and Joel Dahmen, a pair of fan favorites. And Ben Kohles, who’s been hanging around the top of leaderboards since early June while searching for Tour win No. 1. There was also Trace Crowe. He entered Monday’s weather-delayed final round of the Austin Championship with a one-shot lead.

But Saturday, after the third round and before rain washed out Sunday, Chad Ramey said his focus was on Chad Ramey.

“I can’t control how everyone else plays, but I can kind of control what I’m doing,” Ramey said.

And wouldn’t you know, it worked. Ramey is your Austin winner by two shots. He’s also now a two-time Tour winner, and he’s now locked up Tour status for a couple of years, after entering the week at risk of losing it completely — he was 132nd in the season-long points standings, and, after next week, only the top 100 get full-time cards. Monday, he also looked every bit like he was in his own Chad Ramey world, too.

Starting the day a shot back of Crowe, he birdied the par-4 1st after hitting his approach to 4 feet. He birdied the par-4 4th after dropping an 11-foot putt, then the par-5 5th on another 11-footer. On the par-3 11th, he hit his tee shot to 12 feet on his way to birdie. On the par-4 13th, Ramey stuck his second shot to 9 feet en route to birdie, and on the par-5 14th, he was home in two for another birdie.

Then came the par-5 18th. Clinical. A drive into the fairway, an iron well short of the trouble in front of the green, an iron onto the green, and one putt for the birdie. Added all together, that’s a seven-birdie-and-zero-bogey 65, a total of 20-under, and a two-shot victory over Kohles.

“Like I said earlier,” Ramey said, “I came into today just telling myself just mentally stay aggressive. You know, just don’t let up, just stay aggressive.”

Now the Tour heads to its season-ender, at the RSM Classic. And thoughts start to turn to next year.

Ramey never flinched. An impressive display. You can build on that.

– The weather-delayed final round starts with Trace Crowe holding a one-shot lead. Crowe is at 14-under, Chad Ramey, Sami Valimaki and Erik van Rooyen are at 13-under, and Max Greyserman and Ben Kohles are at 12-under.

– As the final group makes the turn, the leaderboard reads this way: Ramey is at 16-under, Kohles, Crowe, Valimaki and Austin Smotherman are at 14-under, and Tommy Morrison, Joel Dahmen, Kristoffer Ventura, Hayden Springer and Zac Blair are at 13-under.

– Springer eagles the 377-yard, par-4 13th hole by holing out from 117 yards away. Ramey is at 16-under, Springer is at 15-under, and Smotherman, Kohles, Crowe and Valimaki are at 14-under.

– Ramey birdies the 218-yard, par-3 11th after hitting his tee shot to 12 feet, and he leads by two. Ramey is at 17-under, Springer is at 15-under, and Smotherman, Dahmen, Kohles, Crowe and Valimaki are at 14-under.

– Springer almost eagles a second-straight hole, but settles for a birdie on the 567-yard, par-5 14th. Ramey is at 17-under, Springer is at 16-under, Kohles is at 15-under, and seven players are at 14-under.

– Ramey birdies the 13th after hitting his approach to 9 feet, and he leads by two. He’s at 18-under, Springer is at 16-under, and Smotherman, Kohles, Crowe and Blades Brown are at 15-under.

– Springer bogeys the 443-yard, par-4 16th, and Kohles birdies the 14th, and the leaderboard now read this way: Ramey is at 18-under, Kohles is at 16-under, and Brown, Smotherman, Springer and Crowe are at 15-under.

– Ramey birdies the 14th after getting home in two, and his lead grows to three. He’s at 19-under, and Brown, Kohles and Crowe are at 16-under.

– Kohles birdies the 443-yard, par-4 16th on a 53-foot putt, and he moves within two shots of the lead. Ramey is at 19-under, Kohles is at 17-under, and Brown, Springer and Crowe are at 16-under.

– Kohles birdies the 561-yard, par-5 18th on a 14-foot putt, and Ramey’s lead is one as heads to his final hole. Ramey is at 19-under, Kohles is at 18-under, and Brown, Springer and Crowe are at 16-under.

– Ramey plays the 18th nearly flawlessly — a drive into the fairway, an iron well short of the trouble in front of the green, an iron to the green and one putt for the birdie. Ramey finishes at 20-under, and he wins by two for his second PGA Tour title.

“Just stay aggressive. That was my mindset going into today. Because every week, somebody is going to go low on Sunday.” — Ramey on Golf Channel after the win

title: After historic Sunday, Rory McIlroy bullish about more than just his own game
article_text:
Sunday in Dubai ended with Rory McIlroy winning an emotional, history-tying eighth Race to Dubai title after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship, five shots behind winner Tyrrell Hatton. The second-place finish saw McIlroy narrowly pass Eugenio Chacarra, the 26-year-old Spaniard who finished tied for fourth, two shots behind McIlroy, for the season-long crown.

The victory left McIlroy emotional. After the win, McIlroy revealed that his father, Gerry, recently underwent a double lung transplant and that he spent nine days in the ICU. Rory said his father is doing well and told him to “go win the Race to Dubai,” which spurred McIlroy to chase down Chacarra and claim his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title. The win further cemented McIlroy’s status as one of, if not the, greatest European golfers in history.

The battle with Chacarra and Hatton in Dubai, as well as the one with Jon Rahm the week before in Abu Dhabi, also left McIlroy beaming with optimism about the future of a different event — one that is deeply ingrained in his DNA: the Ryder Cup.

Chacarra, who was a top amateur when he left for LIV Golf in 2022, has been grinding his way up the professional golf ladder since leaving the rebel league after the 2024 season and has wound up being one of the big winners of golf’s fracture. He won the Hero Indian Open last year to secure full-time status on the DP World Tour and then won three times this year to take the Race to Dubai lead heading into the final two events of the season. While McIlroy eventually tracked down Chacarra on the final day of the season, he sees Chacarra (and his pure ball-striking) as someone who will become a fixture on European Ryder Cup teams.

“He’s a gritty competitor,” McIlroy said of Chacarra on Sunday. “I think you can see that with how he plays and how he goes about it and his — it’s cliché to say, ‘Oh, he’s a fiery Spaniard.’ But he is. That’s sort of who he is, and he plays with his heart on his sleeve and you can see the emotions that he feels out there. I always view these things in the lens of the Ryder Cup, and he’s certainly going to be an asset for Europe in the future for sure.”

After winning the DP World India Championship last month, Chacarra got a congratulatory hug from captain Luke Donald and noted he planned to make the loaded team at Adare Manor next fall without a handout.

“I told Luke back in the day I want to be on that team, not just a pick,” Chacarra said in India. “I want to be one of the six [automatic] spots. So that’s one of the goals we have on the team. I’m working really hard for it. We are still a year away, but I know what I’m capable of. I know I’m a good player. I got a lot of charisma, and I just want to keep getting better and keep winning.”

With five top-four finishes since the Ryder Cup qualification window opened at the end of August, Chacarra currently sits in the top spot as he heads to the PGA Tour in 2027.

Chacarra’s DP World Tour breakthrough season wasn’t the only recent development that has McIlroy feeling good about Team Europe’s present and future.

Rahm and Hatton have been an integral part to Europe’s success in the past two Ryder Cups. Rahm has gone 5-2-2 in Europe’s last two Ryder Cup wins while Hatton has gone 6-0-2. The partnership is 4-0-0 across the last two Ryder Cups. Rahm and Hatton have been key to Europe’s success in the Ryder Cup but their play has been uneven in majors since joining LIV Golf, and the breakaway league’s uncertain future and its impact on their own status weighed on them both over the summer. Both Rahm and Hatton have admitted to dealing with “noise” this season as they tried to navigate their new reality as the once-Saudi-backed league started to crumble.

But once LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September, both players quickly exited the league instead of signing up for LIV Golf 2.0, and LIV has since told the court it will be winding down operations and is no longer pursuing a reboot. That Rahm won in his first start post-LIV and Hatton won in his second is not coincidental to McIlroy, who sees two of his teammates and friends carrying less weight than before which allows them to play their best golf. It also means that Donald won’t have to use a captain’s pick on either since they will be playing on the DP World Tour full-time in 2027, opening up a world of possibilities for a team gunning for a three-peat.

“It’s amazing,” McIlroy said of Rahm and Hatton’s winning return to the DP World Tour. “I think you look at what’s transpired in golf over the last few weeks, you know, Jon coming back, winning in Abu Dhabi. Tyrrell he’s been winning pretty regularly on the European Tour for the last few years, anyway, even when he was playing on LIV. But it’s an amazing — I just think as well for the Ryder Cup Team and points, you want guys like Tyrrell and Jon and that caliber of player to make the team automatically so that Luke wouldn’t have to waste a pick on them, essentially.

title: Rory McIlroy, Scottie Scheffler headline teams for Golf Channel Games
article_text:
Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler once again will headline the team rosters at the Optum Golf Channel Games, which debuted in 2025 and will be held at Trump National Golf Club Jupiter.

The event will be contested on Wednesday, Dec. 16, airing live in primetime on Golf Channel and USA Network.

Tickets are on sale at thegolfchannelgames.com and at TickPick.com.

Team Rory will include 2022 U.S. Open Champion Matt Fitzpatrick, four-time PGA Tour winner Si Woo Kim and four-time DP World Tour winner Haotong Li, who is returning to Team Rory for the 2026 competition.

Team Scottie, which won last year's inaugural Optum Golf Channel Games, will feature Chris Gotterup, a five-time PGA Tour winner including three wins in 2026, three-time PGA Tour winner Michael Brennan and 2026 PGA Tour rookie standout and Tour winner Jackson Koivun.

"The inaugural Optum Golf Channel Games proved that a unique format showcasing the best players in the world under the pressure of a running clock produces a kind of energy we don't normally see in our sport," said Tom Knapp, Golf Channel EVP and GM. "That energy translated to the viewers at home and we're excited to build off of last year's momentum with this group of elite golfers, leaning into what worked well last year and implementing some new challenges this year."

World No. 1 Scheffler and No. 2 McIlroy will be leading their teams through the rapid-fire golf competition, which will feature challenges such as the Team Relay and 14-Club Challenge, as well as new challenges for the 2026 competitors.

- Six of the top 20 players in the Official World Golf Rankings: Scheffler (No. 1), McIlroy (2), Fitzpatrick (3), Gotterup (8), Kim (14) and Brennan (20).

- Three Major Champions: Scheffler, McIlroy, Fitzpatrick.

IOC seeks new South Korean broadcast partner as JTBC drops Olympic rights
article_text:
JTBC, the debt-ridden South Korean broadcaster, has terminated its rights agreement with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) covering the Winter and Summer Games through 2032 as part of its rehabilitation plan.

In a statement, JTBC said it hoped the move would “eliminate financial uncertainty and establish a stable management foundation,” adding that it would “continue to communicate closely with the IOC through various channels to address outstanding matters arising from the termination of the agreement,” including remaining broadcast rights fees.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The company said it expects another broadcaster or consortium to secure the rights for the remaining events on the contract, including the upcoming 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, the 2030 Alps Winter Olympics, and the 2032 Brisbane Olympics.

The broadcaster added: “The costs resulting from the termination will be determined through the third quarter accounting process and in accordance with the rehabilitation plan once it is approved.

“By accounting for the expected losses as part of the rehabilitation process, we aim to remove financial uncertainty and sustain growth in operating profit from our core businesses.”

JTBC secured exclusive broadcasting rights covering four Olympic events between 2026 and 2032 after securing a contract with the IOC in June 2019.

The broadcaster had initially planned to resell its Olympic rights to major Korean broadcasters, but negotiations broke down, leaving JTBC to bear the cost of solely broadcasting the games.

JTBC also picked up exclusive rights in the country to soccer’s flagship World Cups between 2026 and 2030 in a deal reportedly worth $250 million. The agreement covers the 2030 edition of the men's soccer tournament and the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2027.

Sublicensing this year’s World Cup also faced difficulties, but KBS eventually agreed to purchase rights to jointly air the tournament.

The financial burden of both rights contracts ultimately led to the company filing for corporate rehabilitation proceedings with the Seoul Bankruptcy Court last June.

In August, a Seoul court approved the broadcaster’s request to begin rehabilitation proceedings, allowing the company to restructure its debts under court supervision.

Earlier this month, JTBC officially started the company’s sale process, with the aim of selecting a preferred bidder in January.

Tamaiti Williams reaches major milestone in recovery from disc-eating infection
article_text:
Tamaiti Williams has reached a significant milestone in his recovery from the back infection that ended his 2026 season after just two games for the Crusaders: running.

The All Blacks prop has been sidelined since discovering that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) had been eating a disc in his lower back, causing immense pain and putting more than just his rugby career in jeopardy.

Following a surgical procedure that included fusing two discs together, Williams has been slowly progressing through a lengthy rehab process as he eyes an eventual return to rugby.

The 26-year-old was named in the Crusaders’ 2027 squad, but with an injury replacement in Frenchman Clément Castets, signalling he is expected to miss at least part of the coming season.

One month later, Williams’ timeline remains uncertain, but the club shared a promising update to their social media channels on Thursday afternoon. The 27-Test All Black was shown jogging on a treadmill while attached to a load-sharing machine, which was holding 25 per cent of his body weight to ease the stress on his lower body and back.

“I feel fit. I feel light,” he said, grinning in the video. “It feels pretty foreign, though. I haven’t run since March, before all of the chaos happened. It feels good, though. No pain, which is good.”

Williams said his body “feels good” after his first run in eight months, adding: “We’ll get our recovery done and then we’ll go again.”

Crusaders physio John Roche was by Williams’ side for the milestone, and was thrilled to see it all go smoothly.

“This piece of kit is pretty amazing; it weighs the athlete, and then we can adjust the percentage of body weight so they can run at less than their full body weight. So, Tams is running at 75 per cent of his body weight at the moment.

“The treadmill can go up to 30 kilometres an hour, so you can run fast, but obviously he’s not going to do that for his first run. It’s just great to see the big man up and running.”

title: All Blacks to address mentality concerns ahead of decisive England Test
article_text:
All Blacks forwards coach Jason Ryan emerged from Saturday’s historic loss to Wales with questions over his team’s mentality in the match, questions he intends to answer ahead of a decisive Test against England at Twickenham this weekend.

New Zealand were beaten by a remarkable Welsh performance in the penultimate round of Nations Championship pool play that made more tackles than any team before them in Test history, but also came out of the gates firing on attack under the roof at Principality Stadium.

The All Blacks spent most of the final quarter of the Test pummeling the Welsh line, but were given no reward as Wales repelled their efforts and held them up any time they crossed the whitewash. The defensive display earned Ryan’s praise, but it was his side’s lack of energy that he kept coming back to in his immediate post-game reaction.

“It’s disappointing. It’s going to hurt for a while, that one,” Ryan told Jason Pine on Newstalk ZB shortly after the final whistle in Cardiff. “We just didn’t finish the opportunities we had, and they started the game with more intensity than us, and then started the second half with more intensity than us.

“And then, effectively, their defence, we just couldn’t break them down. Credit to them, and they deserve their win.”

Ryan said that after the slow start and Wales taking the lead, his players “went into their shells a little”, keeping Wales on top in the Test.

“We just didn’t come out of the blocks. We did the short kick-off and never regained that, and then they converted straight away and got momentum and bang. Teams score so fast now. But we were under pressure, and we couldn’t get ourselves out of it. And that’s probably the most disappointing thing.

“I’m just disappointed because we can’t hide from the fact that there are potentially parts in that game we’d have to question, mentally, if we were there. I think last week was a massive emotional week for us as a whole team and a whole group, and potentially we might have just been a little bit blasé of how we rolled up into Cardiff and got smacked for it.”

The team is still grieving the unexpected loss of their head of security, Logan Cadwallader, who had been with them for 10 years.

Ryan was adamant the All Blacks did not underestimate Wales’ quality, but admitted they did make life difficult for themselves with their selections. With an inaugural Nations Championship final now just two weeks away, the forwards coach was eager to rebound swiftly.

“Oh no, I don’t think it’s complacency. I just think they started and we just couldn’t pull them back, and that is what it is. We’ve got to move forward. We’ve got to move forward quickly.

“We also made a lot of changes; I think it was 10 that we made, and that’s cohesion. We gave a lot of fellas an opportunity, and there are some pretty good boys sitting in the stands, experience-wise, and potentially we lacked a bit of that at the end as well.

“I think we just have to have a look at it and just see where we were mentally; how we started the Test match.

“You’ve got to say that some of the defensive sets that Wales did were honestly quite unbelievable, and they were pretty spirited, and they hung in there and hung in there, and we just couldn’t break them down. So credit to them, they deserve that one.”

title: USA U20 star among four uncapped players in Australia’s Dubai Sevens squad
article_text:
USA Under-20s centre Dane Mitchell and former Moana Pasifika outside back Denzel Samoa are set to make their Australia Sevens debuts next week, with four uncapped players named to play at the HSBC SVNS Series season opener in Dubai.

Global Youth Sevens standout Bailey Roberts-Lintmeijer and ACT Brumbies prospect Chayse Geros have also been selected. Coach Liam Barry has otherwise gone with a fairly experienced group, which boasts a combined 235 SVNS events between them.

Mitchell made five appearances for the USA at the World Rugby Junior World Championship in Georgia, which included a few starts. But after returning to Australia, the university student got a chance to trial for the sevens side, which has opened the door to travelling the world.

Three-time Olympian Henry Hutchison is the most experienced member of the squad, having played at 68 tournaments, which Maurice Longbottom and James Turner bring more leadership to the national team.

Nathan Lawson is back with the sevens side after a stint in the NRL, having played a handful of matches for the St George Illawarra Dragons. Ben Dalton and Jayden Blake are others who have played in at least 10 events.

Australia will be without a few big-name players for the first stop of the season, with Henry Paterson still sidelined with a knee injury. Will Cartwright (knee) and Ben Dowling (foot) are also unavailable for selection.

“The squad has had a good few weeks in preparation and we are looking forward to our first tournament in Dubai,” Australia Men’s Sevens coach Liam Barry said.

“The 2026/2027 season has the added factor of Olympic qualification so we are well aware of the importance of getting off to a good start.”

Australia kick off their SVNS Series against the USA, South Africa and Argentina, If selected, Mitchell could potentially debut in the green and gold against the United States – who he was eligible for due to his mother.

The Aussies finished the 2025/26 SVNS Series strong with a drought-breaking title in Valladolid. SVNS Series action is stopping by the same destinations as last season, with Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, New York and Vancouver hosting regular season stops.

It’s a particularly important season with the top four teams securing automatic qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The World Championship heads to Hong Kong China, Valladolid and Bordeaux.

title: Wallaroos breakout star set for Australia Sevens debut in Dubai
article_text:
World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year nominee Amelia Whitaker will soon fly to Dubai as the only uncapped player in the Australia Women’s Sevens side, who are looking to win the HSBC SVNS Series event for the sixth time in seven years.

Whitaker was named the NSW Waratahs Player of the Year after a stellar Super Rugby Women’s campaign, and the winger was rewarded with higher Wallaroos honours. The 20-year-old rounded out a career-best 15s season with some stellar performances against Scotland.

Prolific Wallaroos try-scorers Desiree Miller and Maya Stewart were joined in the back three by Whitaker, who received Player of the Match honours after scoring two tries in a 56-12 win over Scotland at Sydney’s Accor Stadium.

The Wallaroos kicked off a historic quadruple header at Stadium Australia, with all four Teams in Gold taking the field. Australia faced arch-rivals the Black Ferns Sevens for the third time in less than 24 hours, while Whitaker celebrated with the Wallaroos.

Those SVNS Series players are now Whitaker’s teammates, with Isabella Nasser captaining a side that boasts World Championship-winning experience. Australia took out titles in Valladolid and Bordeaux earlier this year, as they pipped New Zealand in the race for the circuit’s top prize.

Maddison Levi is nearing the all-time try-scoring on the SVNS Series, with the recent Wallaroos debutant looking to chase down New Zealand’s Michalea Brake, who was named in the Black Ferns Sevens squad on Wednesday.

Tia Hinds, Heidi Dennis, Amahli Hala, Teagan Levi, Kaitlin Shave, Kahli Henwood, Bienne Terita, Ruby Nicholas, Kiiahla Duff and Alysia Lefau-Fakosilea have been named. MacKenzie Davis and Faith Nathan are unavailable due to injury.

“The team has had a strong preparation, with plenty of rugby played in different competitions and environments as well as two high-level tournaments together as a squad,” coach Reg Tayler said.

“We have benefited from these experiences and have been able to bring them back some learnings into our environment.

“We’ve got a good balance of youth and experience, and we’re heading to Dubai and Cape Town to set the standard.”

Australia started their SVNS Series matches against France, the USA and Spain in pool play. While New Zealand are the defending champions, the Aussies had won five straight titles at the event before that.

title: HSBC SVNS 3 pools locked in as teams eye promotion to second tier
article_text:
The Canadian Men’s Sevens side are heading back to Dubai this month, looking to defend their HSBC SVNS 3 crown against five challengers. But with only two sides able to progress to the second tier, there’s plenty at stake on November 27-28.

Canada wrapped up the inaugural SVNS 3 title by overcoming Belgium in January, while Samoa wrapped up third place. Samoa will look to go at least one better this time around, as teams look to take another step towards the SVNS World Championship.

The six-team men’s and women’s pools have now been confirmed, following the conclusion of regional qualification tournaments. Canada and Samoa are joined by Chile, Hong Kong China, Italy and Zimbabwe in the men’s group.

South Africa defeated Argentina in the women’s decider 11 months ago, but a first-time champion will be crowned in just over one week. China, Colombia, Mexico, Poland, Samoa and Uganda will battle it out for a sought-after top-two finish.

“The return of HSBC SVNS 3 to Dubai is another important moment for the development of international rugby sevens and our ambition to create meaningful opportunities for more nations to compete on the global stage,” World Rugby Sevens World Series General Manager Sam Pinder said last month.

“Bringing HSBC SVNS 3 together with HSBC SVNS provides a fantastic platform to showcase the depth of talent across the game, from teams looking to take the next step to the world’s best competing at the highest level.

“With promotion to HSBC SVNS 2 at stake, there is plenty to play for, and we’re looking forward to an exciting weekend of rugby sevens in Dubai.”

The two best teams will earn promotion through to HSBC SVNS 2, while will be played over three events early next year. Nairobi, Sao Paulo and Montevideo will host tournaments for the second season in a row, with World Championship spots on the line.

Dubai will host SVNS 3 and the opening stop of the first division SVNS Series, which features the top eight men’s and women’s teams in the world. New Zealand are looking to go back-to-back after claiming silverware at The Sevens Stadium 12 months ago.

The Series will also visit Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, Vancouver and New York, before the World Championship in April and May. World Championship tournaments will be played in Hong Kong China, Valladolid and Bordeaux once again.

title: Alexander Zverev notified of lawsuit by former partner in abuse case during middle of ATP Finals
article_text:
World No 1 Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday.

The latest legal case brought by the mother of Zverev's former partner alleges the tennis player violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports news outlet L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven."

Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement shared with The Associated Press that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit on Wednesday.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit," Zverev's lawyers said. "If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion" protected by the German constitution.

They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, told The Associated Press that Zverev's claim over his innocence "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client."

He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honour had been violated.

"Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form," he said. "Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement."

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and that he be fined up to £208,484 €250,000 euros every time if he does.

Zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to Patea during an argument in Berlin in May 2020. He always denied any wrongdoing.

The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement. Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organisations.

Zverev this month ascended to the No 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and is competing this week at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Zverev has not commented on the lawsuit.

He previously denied abuse allegations from another former girlfriend, Olga Sharypova, who first made the accusations in 2020 and followed up in 2021 with a detailed account in a Slate.com article that was taken down because of a preliminary injunction issued by a German court. Slate said it stood by the article.

The allegations prompted the men's professional tennis tour, the ATP, to investigate her claims. It ended 15 months later, in January 2023, with the ATP saying there was "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

title: ‘I see comments every day’: Sonay Kartal’s fightback against injury and online abuse
article_text:
Sonay Kartal believes the vitriolic abuse and threats that she and her fellow players receive after every match have become an unavoidable part of her job.

“Unfortunately, it’s something that comes with the sport,” the British No 2 says. “I don’t really have a choice to not deal with it. Obviously, it’s not a good thing to have and as a player, win or lose, you’re seeing those things.

“You can try and take yourself away from it as much as you can and you can do different things to your [social media] account to try and hide it, but it’s a shame that it is something we have to deal with and hopefully it can change. But we’ve all been there, we know what it’s like when you have a loss and you see your social media flooded with not very nice comments.”

Social media abuse has been a constant theme for players in recent years, particularly due to the prevalence of sports betting, and many have spoken out. Most recently, her compatriot Jodie Burrage reposted some of the barrage of abuse received on her Instagram account earlier this month.

While the governing bodies have developed some tools to monitor it, and limit the comments that players see, Kartal notes that most of those initiatives come at the cost of privacy, making them a less than ideal solution. “I see those comments every day, it’s hard to avoid them,” she says.

“You look at a post, you look at your Instagram, and they’re there. At the start, it was not very nice to read but unfortunately I’m used to it now so it’s just another one. You just deal with it. It is what it is.”

Kartal was speaking from the comfort of the National Tennis Centre, her home away from home, at the end of perhaps the most challenging season of her career. In March, she defeated the 2025 Australian Open champion, Madison Keys, to reach the last 16 at Indian Wells, an excellent result. At No 54 in the world rankings, she sat 10 spots away from her career-high No 44 and it seemed she would keep on moving forward. Instead, she would not compete for another six months after being diagnosed with a stress fracture in her back.

As she reflects on months of long rehab and the frustration of working through her injury at Roehampton while surrounded by players sweeping in and out between tournaments, Kartal describes the first month as the most painful. “It was just very uncomfortable,” she says. “I had a lot of nerve pain, too. I wouldn’t wish sciatica pain upon anyone. Back pain and nerve pain is not fun.

“I would just be doing normal things like brushing my teeth or putting my shoes on and I’m in quite a lot of pain, which is not fun. For a 24-year-old it was not something I really wanted to deal with, which is another reason why I just had to let this get better. I couldn’t really rush it because it’s six months of my time now versus maybe it’s post-Sonay’s tennis life constantly having back pain.”

Her response was spectacular. While some players naturally take time to find their timing or match instincts after such a long time out, Kartal hit the ground running immediately. In just her third tournament back at the Wuhan Open in October, she defeated Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko, four former top-five players, consecutively to reach her first WTA 1000 final – and led Maja Chwalinska in the final before being beaten in three sets.

Having tumbled to No 170 in the world that week due to her extended absence, that result allowed her ranking to skyrocket, and she is now at No 53 as she prepares for the new season. She also briefly became the British No 1 – Katie Boulter has since leapfrogged her once more – for the first time.

Kartal’s next goal is to be seeded at the major tournaments and, having dragged herself so quickly back to where she was before the injury, to keep on pushing forward: “I didn’t worry about ever getting back to that level,” she says, shrugging. “I just wasn’t sure how long it would take me.”

title: UK firms owed thousands as Saudi-backed LIV paid golfers millions
article_text:
LIV Golf - backed by more than $5bn (£3.8bn) from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund - paid millions to players and executives in the weeks before filing for bankruptcy, while leaving a trail of unpaid bills from UK suppliers.

BBC Sport has seen invoices from five small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, all of which were overdue before LIV made its final payments to players.

Global Infusion Group,, external a Buckinghamshire company that provided catering at July's LIV Golf UK event, is still owed £321,671, due on 7 August.

Suffolk-based BD365 Clean, external provided 108 cleaning staff and is owed £75,225, most of which was due on 20 July and 13 August.

"It just feels completely immoral," said Bonnie May, chief executive of Global Infusion Group.

"It really matters to a business of our scale. The impact has been huge, both personally and professionally."

Only $2m (£1.5m) has been earmarked so far by the Saudi owners to pay unsecured creditors, leaving many smaller companies unsure if they will receive anything at all.

Yet court filings reveal LIV made 59 payments to golfers on 31 July, amounting to $16.6m (£12.6m) and matching prize money for the same LIV Golf UK event.

A further $34.2m (£25.9m) went to players between 17 August and 3 September following tournaments in New York and Indianapolis, including $6.4m (£4.9m) to 2026 champion Jon Rahm just five days before the bankruptcy filing.

Four senior LIV executives also received retention bonuses totalling nearly $3m (£2.3m) in August.

"It's sickening," said Krissi Foskett, owner of BD365 Clean, who described the unpaid bills as "almost an extinction-level event" for her team.

"How can they sleep at night, knowing they are potentially putting companies out of business?"

Meanwhile, public records list more than £3,000 owed to Goodysphere,, external a family-run Yorkshire firm that provides a sensory bus designed to help autistic children who may find busy events overwhelming.

LIV Golf did not respond to our request for comment.

However, in August, LIV chief executive Scott O'Neil said he hoped they would be able to pay their suppliers.

"What I would say to them is we're doing everything we can to make sure we can do right by them and the work they committed."

The controversial breakaway league had been owned and bankrolled by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) since its launch season in 2022.

But in April, the fund announced it would end its backing after the 2026 season, putting LIV's future in doubt.

"Our understanding was that the funding would take LIV through 2026," said Global Infusion Group's May, whose company had about 60 staff catering for players and broadcasters.

"We weren't aware the funding had already stopped and there wasn't enough to actually fulfil their obligations."

PIF's multi-billion-dollar investment helped it to lure some of golf's biggest names and disrupt the PGA Tour's dominance of the sport.

"It's Saudi money, that's safe as houses, we thought," said Foskett.

"Their head honchos came along and enjoyed hospitality. We were there cleaning up at one o'clock in the morning then back in at five in the morning, only to be treated like this."

PIF remains the majority owner of Newcastle United, while Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 Fifa World Cup.

"I'm sure the country won't want to be saddled with the characterisation that it doesn't pay its bills," said professor Simon Chadwick, who is an expert in the business and politics of sport across Africa, Europe and Asia.

"I do find it surprising that they would simply walk away. I think they would want to engage in some kind of remedial action, particularly in terms of managing their image and reputation."

Filmmaker Joe Bentley spent eight days from April working on a video for LIV's YouTube channel that is still online.

He is owed nearly £6,000, with £2,226 due on 31 July.

The video was part of the 'LIV Back' series, set up to "focus on the impact LIV players and teams are making off the course".

He filmed at two schools taking part in 'Little Sticks', a LIV outreach programme which aimed to provide golf equipment and training in areas of deprivation.

"You feel massively deflated, a bit cheated and undervalued," said Bentley.

"Everyone I dealt with at LIV was lovely. The first email I sent chasing was to a production coordinator or a manager and even she was appalled that we hadn't been paid."

Gateshead Council is also owed £1,912, due on 22 August, relating to 'Little Sticks'.

"Transformation is not a short-term process," said Professor Chadwick.

"If you're going to embark on investment programmes in community sport, grassroots sport, you've got to make a long-term commitment and those changes have got to take place."

"The contacts we had sadly all lost their jobs," said Giles Mitchell, whose company, Office Pantry, supplied food to LIV's office on London's South Bank.

"We didn't hear anything from them and then their emails started bouncing back."

There was hope the competition could survive in some form with new investment, but in November LIV announced it was winding down operations.

In the bankruptcy filings, LIV estimated it had between $500m and $1bn (£380m-£760m) in liabilities and at least 1,000 creditors.

The largest 30 unsecured creditors alone were listed with claims of more than $64m (£49m).

"I think the message is loud and clear to somebody like me that, no, we're not going to get paid for any of this," said May.

title: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour following LIV Golf collapse
article_text:
Two-time US Open champion Bryson DeChambeau has agreed to join the DP World Tour for next season.

DeChambeau was among a host of star names who joined LIV Golf four years ago and maintained his commitment even after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing for the breakaway tour in April.

Earlier this month the 33-year-old American said he "gave everything" to keep LIV Golf alive as the tour confirmed its intention to wind down operations.

As first reported in the Telegraph,, external DeChambeau successfully submitted his application to join the European Tour before Sunday's deadline.

DeChambeau has already confirmed he will compete in Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge - a DP World Tour event - in South Africa in December.

As a recent major champion DeChambeau has been given 'category one' membership by the DP World Tour, which means he is guaranteed entry to any event across the season.

Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson - other former major champions who defected to LIV - have signed agreements to receive invitations to a specific number of tournaments.

Veteran English trio Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Paul Casey, plus Northern Ireland's Graeme McDowell, are among a number of ex-LIV players who are eligible to play on the DP World Tour in 2027.

The full-time return of Spain's Jon Rahm and England's Tyrrell Hatton, who did not resign their memberships, has also been confirmed.

"There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months," said DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings.

"As golf's global tour, we have taken a pragmatic approach to this unique and unprecedented situation as we go into next year, always with the best interests of our entire membership at the forefront of our minds."

As one of the poster boys of LIV Golf, and one of the biggest names in the sport, it was intriguing to see what DeChambeau would do next.

With LIV golfers automatically banned for a year by the PGA Tour, it was thought he might decide to focus on his YouTube and social media channels - which have attracted a new, younger audience of many millions - over the next 12 months.

But joining the DP World Tour is a logical option for the big-hitting American, who reportedly received £95m, external to join LIV in 2022 and earned almost £50m in prize money over four seasons.

Signing up for the European-based tour means he can play the traditional format of the game on a regular basis and offers a pathway back to the PGA Tour.

The leading 10 players on the DP World Tour in a season are guaranteed PGA Tour cards for the following season, which was a route taken by Patrick Reed - DeChambeau's former US Ryder Cup team-mate - when he left LIV before the start of the 2026 season.

For the DP World Tour, DeChambeau brings further star power to their product.

DeChambeau will join the likes of European superstars Rory McIlroy and Tommy Fleetwood as full-time members, and boosts the tour's stock as the golfing landscape continues to realign following LIV's demise.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy said earlier this month.

Six-time major champion McIlroy also claimed those connected to LIV were expressing an ambition to "destroy the European Tour" during this year's Masters.

Instead, the Saudi-backed venture is to be liquidated and has led to an influx of big-names joining the DP World Tour.

As well as DeChambeau being given membership for the first time, it was announced that Johnson, Smith and Watson are among a group of nine former LIV players allowed to play a limited number of events.

They will be picked at the discretion of the DP World Tour to "add value to those tournaments", which is designed to prevent full-time members from missing playing opportunities.

On allowing former LIV players to join the tour, Kinnings added: "We realise there are different viewpoints.

"But this approach, discussed and agreed with our tournament committee and allied to this responsibly managed programme of invites, will add value which, in turn, will benefit the tour as a whole."

title: Snapdragon Bets On F1's Youngest-Ever Champion To Sharpen Sports Marketing Returns For Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM)
article_text:
When Kimi Antonelli claimed the Formula 1 World Championship title this month at just 20 years old, chipmaker Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) already had him under contract.

Qualcomm’s consumer-facing brand Snapdragon had signed Antonelli as a brand ambassador, a move now anchored by a new anthem film timed to the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 21.

The campaign marks a deliberate shift in how Qualcomm approaches sports sponsorship, prioritizing measurable returns over the prestige-driven partnerships the company pursued in previous years.

Snapdragon’s current deal with the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 team, of which Antonelli is a driver, launched in 2023 and was built from the outset around marketing accountability.

That contrasts sharply with Qualcomm’s earlier Mercedes partnership from the 2010s, which CMO Don McGuire acknowledged was not “ROI-driven, marketing-driven” in its orientation.

McGuire, who took the CMO role in 2021, is now overseeing a strategy that extends the brand relationship from content and storytelling into activations and hospitality.

“We believe we’re already seeing higher ROI coming out of some things that we’ve done in the short term,” McGuire said, signaling confidence in the retooled approach.

One structural challenge facing the campaign is Apple TV’s exclusive U.S. broadcast rights to F1, which blocks brands like Snapdragon from placing traditional television ads around domestic race coverage.

Rather than treating that as a ceiling, the brand is routing the anthem film through Sky broadcasts outside the United States, alongside digital placements and partnerships with Sports Illustrated and YouTube.

“We’ve got other ways to bring it to life,” McGuire said of the campaign’s distribution strategy around the Las Vegas race.

Antonelli’s historic championship adds significant organic reach to the partnership, as the Italian driver’s record-breaking season has drawn sustained global media attention throughout the year.

Snapdragon’s sports marketing ambitions extend well beyond the paddock, with the brand also holding a sponsorship deal with what McGuire describes as the world’s biggest soccer property.

That soccer partnership has generated what McGuire called “humongous ROI,” and it now serves as the internal benchmark against which all other sports deals are measured.

“When you’re dealing with a sports brand that big, at scale, the brand can withstand the ebbs and flows of performance on the pitch because the fan base is so huge,” McGuire explained.

He added: “That’s the benchmark that we use [for sports partnerships] and maybe it’s a little unfair because they are arguably the biggest sports brand in the world.”

The Antonelli signing reflects a broader industry trend of brands pursuing younger, generationally resonant athletes as Formula 1 continues expanding its commercial footprint in North America.

title: Gctc Announces New Naming Rights Partnership
NASCAR Lands Major Sponsorship Deal for 2027 Chase Race
article_text:
Watkins Glen International is getting a new race sponsor to go along with its return to NASCAR's championship stretch.

The New York road course announced Monday that Busch Light will serve as the entitlement sponsor of its 2027 NASCAR Cup Series race, officially naming the event Busch Light at The Glen.

https://twitter.com/WGI/status/2122435803120832560

Scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 19, the race will hold particular significance on next season's calendar. Watkins Glen will be the only road course featured in the 2027 NASCAR Chase, putting a premium on road racing talent as drivers compete for the Cup Series championship.

For Busch Light, the agreement gives one of NASCAR's most recognizable commercial partners an even greater presence during the most consequential portion of the season.

Few beer brands have as deep a history in stock car racing as Busch.

A longtime supporter of the sport, Busch Light currently serves as a Premier Partner and the Official Beer Sponsor of NASCAR. The brand also sponsors the Busch Light Pole Award, giving it a consistent presence throughout the Cup Series season.

Its latest investment puts the brand's name on one of the most anticipated road course races of 2027.

"Busch Light has been part of NASCAR race weekends for decades, and we're proud to deepen that connection as entitlement partner of Busch Light at The Glen," said Krystyn Stowe, head of marketing, Busch Family & Natural Family at Anheuser-Busch.

The financial terms of the sponsorship were not disclosed in the announcement.

After hosting its Cup Series race in May in 2026, Watkins Glen will return to a fall race date next season with considerably more at stake.

As the lone road course on the Chase schedule, the 2.45-mile circuit presents a vastly different challenge for championship contenders accustomed to competing on ovals.

"With The Glen returning to The Chase in 2027, we're proud to build on our road racing tradition together and welcome fans to the Finger Lakes for a fall weekend with championship stakes," Watkins Glen International President Dawn Burlew said.

- Friday, Sept. 17: ARCA Menards Series race

- Saturday, Sept. 18: NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Mission Foods 200 at The Glen

- Sunday, Sept. 19: NASCAR Cup Series Busch Light at The Glen

Tickets and camping packages for the 2027 race weekend are already on sale through Watkins Glen International.

For the New York circuit, a nationally recognized title sponsor and a race with championship implications make for a particularly attractive combination heading into 2027.

title: Nadine Roos leads injury returnees as Springboks target SVNS 2 success
article_text:
Springbok Women’s Sevens head coach Cecil Afrika has received a major boost ahead of the HSBC SVNS 2 campaign, with star playmaker Nadine Roos returning from injury.

Roos, named SA Rugby Women’s Player of the Year in 2025 after helping the Springbok Women reach their first-ever Women’s Rugby World Cup quarter-final, missed the majority of 2026 after suffering an injury in SVNS 2 action in March as the side placed third in Montevideo.

As a result, Roos missed HSBC SVNS World Championship events in Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux as the Springbok Women’s Sevens failed to get a top-eight finish and a HSBC SVNS Series spot.

“That was my first very serious injury, but I made peace with the injury early on,” Roos said.

“I realised that it would take a certain amount of time and managing the recovery was key. Returning to the field with the sevens squad – where my career started – was also a full circle moment for me.”

Roos is not the only returnee to the training pitch. Rights Mkhari, Liske Lategan, Leigh Fortuin, Shannon-Lee Windvogel and Kemisetso Baloyi have all made returns from long-term injury.

The group will now be available for the new SVNS 2 campaign, which starts in Nairobi this January. The group will then play events in Montevideo and São Paulo, with a top four finish securing a spot at World Championship events.

This year, a top eight finish after three World Championship legs can qualify teams for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Minjon Ras, team doctor, said: “As a medical and rehabilitation team, we’re privileged to work with players who push boundaries and do everything they can to get back to the game they love ahead of schedule.

“Sometimes we have to rein in that eagerness, and sometimes they surprise us. What I admire most is how they trust the rehab process and respect the timeframes we set for them.”

title: Springboks coach invites fans to watch party amid six-game ban
article_text:
Rassie Erasmus has issued an invite to Springboks fans to join a watch party he is hosting online for South Africa’s Nations Championship test against Ireland.

The coach is unable to attend the match due to a six-game ban he copped after a match-fixing rant following South Africa’s loss to France last week.

Under the rules of the ban, he will be unable to enter the stadium, communicate directly or indirectly with players or members of his staff during the match.

The ban will be in effect until a misconduct hearing is conducted per the request of South Africa Rugby. That will not happen before the Ireland game, though.

It is not the first time the outspoken coach has been hit with a ban for his explosive comments, but this time around he is taking a different approach to keep track of his team’s performance and also engage the fans.

The answer: a virtual watch party with the fans.

“Can sit and moan or make the best of it,” Erasmus wrote on X.

“I’ll be watching the match at the hotel, not keen to watch on my own. So let’s give it a go and hope I get the tech sorted – TV on, my laptop camera on and you’re welcome to join me.”

The website for the game-day watch along states the livestream is not an official Springbok or South Africa Rugby event.

Erasmus reiterated it is a “personal, not official” event on his social media pages, inviting fans over the age of 18 to join the stream.

The Springboks will face Ireland at 3.40am AEDT on Sunday, November 22.

title: Ash Barty and Shingo Kunieda to be Inducted Into International Tennis Hall of Fame
article_text:
Major moments inspired all-court conviction in Ashleigh Barty.

Former world No. 1 Barty brought her best in Grand Slam finals posting a 3-0 record in Slam showdowns winning six of the seven sets she played in those finals.

Now, the 30-year-old Barty will receive tennis ultimate honor: Induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Barty and Shingo Kunieda, the most decorated men’s wheelchair tennis player in history, winning a record 28 Grand Slam singles titles and 50 major titles overall, form the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027, the Hall announced today.

The Class of 2027 will be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame during Hall of Fame weekend August 26–28, 2027 in Newport, Rhode Island.

The Barty Party peaked in a homecoming crescendo in January of 2022 as the top-seeded Aussie’s 6-3, 7-6 win over feisty American Danielle Collins snapped a 44-year home singles drought at the Australian Open and captivated Aussies.

Barty’s triumph drew a peak viewership of 4.26 million TV viewers Down Under making it the most widely-viewed Australian Open women’s final in Australia in history.

“I’m so grateful. Tennis has given me everything and more,” Barty said. “In my career, I’ve been introduced and connect with so many amazing people around the world. And it’s also given me the opportunity to have some of my dreams after tennis: Starting a family…

One of the greatest sub 5’8″ servers in tennis history, Barty was a highly-skilled all-court player who excelled on all surfaces.

Barty owns three Grand Slam titles on three different surfaces: 2022 Australian Open on hard court, 2021 Wimbledon on grass and 2019 Roland Garros on clay. Barty’s 114 consecutive weeks as world No. 1 is fourth on the all-time list behind only Serena Williams and Steffi Graf (186 consecutive weeks apiece) and Martina Navratilova (156 consecutive weeks).

When Barty won the 2021 Wimbledon, she joined Ann Jones, Martina Hingis and Amelie Mauresmo as the fourth junior champion to raise the Rosewater Dish. Barty was such a gifted athlete she played two sports professionally: Cricket and tennis. Barty took the entire 2015 season off and played pro cricket for the Brisbane Heat during her time away from tennis.

“To be able to win Wimbledon which was my dream, my one true dream that I wanted in tennis, really changed my perspective,” Barty said when she announced her 2022 retirement. “I just had that gut feeling after Wimbledon. I had spoken to my team quite a lot about it and there was just a little part of me that wasn’t quite fulfilled.

“Then came the challenge of the Australian Open. That for me just feels like my perfect way to celebrate what an amazing journey my tennis career has been. As a person, this is what I want.”

title: Brooks Koepka: American labels his 2026 PGA Tour season a 'disappointment' and targets 2027 Ryder Cup spot
article_text:
Brooks Koepka has dubbed his 2026 season a "a disappointment" but insists he is hungry to secure a spot on Team USA's 2027 Ryder Cup squad.

The American returned to the PGA Tour via the one-time-only Returning Member Program in January following his LIV Golf exit at the end of 2025, a decision he said he was "beyond happy with".

After being welcomed back to the tour with open arms, Koepka made his return at the Farmers Insurance Open in February. He'd go on to make 16 starts on the PGA Tour this year but would miss the cut at five events and record only one top-10 finish.

- DeChambeau joins DP World Tour: What does it mean for men's golf?

- What golf is live on Sky Sports and when? Full TV listings

Koepka, who was not selected as one of Keegan Bradley's captain's picks for the 2025 Ryder Cup and was also omitted from Brandt Snedeker's President's Cup team in 2026, hopes to raise his game and earn a spot in the roster for next year's Ryder Cup.

"Adare Manor is a big goal of mine," Koepka said. "But this year has just been a little bit of a disappointment, so I know I need to pick it up a little bit.

"It's something I don't enjoy, sitting back watching the Presidents Cup.

"I know I've only played in one [2017], a lot of those [omissions are due to] injuries. But those team events are a lot of fun, I really enjoy them.

"Getting to be around the guys and representing your country is pretty cool.

"So, anytime you can do that, or you have the opportunity to, and you're not able to go play, it kind of infuriates me sitting on the sidelines."

The 36-year-old has featured in four Ryder Cup's in the past, notably helping Team USA to victory in at Hazletine in 2016 and Whistling Straits in 2020.

He boasts an overall individual record of 7-6-2.

Koepka was the lone player to elect to sign up to the PGA Tour's Returning Member Program, with Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith all snubbing the deal, instead choosing to remain at LIV Golf in 2026.

However, following the dissolution of the formerly Saudi-backed breakaway league, Rahm, DeChambeau and Smith have all elected to rejoin the DP World Tour for the 2027 season, along with multiple other former LIV Golf players.

Koepka, meanwhile, was asked ahead of this week's RSM Classic whether he felt back at home after returning to the PGA Tour, replying: "Yeah, I felt very at peace with coming back.

"The reception was fantastic from all the players, caddies, just everybody on tour.

"I think I kept a good relationship with everybody even when I left.

"I think that played probably a huge part in that.

"Everybody was really receptive. I loved the conversations that I've had just throughout the year, just guys asking what was going on, thought process and how things went and the decisions made to get back here.

"Everything was great. I'm beyond happy with my decision."

title: McGinley Warns Of Crowded DP World Tour Field In 2028
article_text:
Paul McGinley, the former European Ryder Cup captain, has issued a stark warning about the future of the DP World Tour. He believes the return of 30 world-class players from the LIV Golf circuit will squeeze out current members by the 2028 season. The former captain spoke to Sky Sports on Tuesday about the math involved in this massive shift. After Bryson DeChambeau and others secured their spots, he told the outlet that "there are no winners in this whole scenario"

Bryson DeChambeau is the most high-profile name to return, earning Category 1 status through his 2022 and 2024 U.S. Open wins. This status lets him play in any event he chooses. These deals exclude Rolex Series events, per reports. The tour says these spots will "add value to those tournaments" while trying to keep things fair for existing members.

McGinley focused his concern on the year 2028 rather than the immediate 2027 season. He explained that the flood of talent will consume a huge chunk of available playing cards. "Because you've got 30 really world-class players coming back to play on the DP World Tour next year from LIV, and they're probably going to take 20 or 30 of the 100 cards that are available," McGinley said. This leaves significantly fewer spots for players who stayed loyal during the split.

LIV defectors received massive financial guarantees that the regulars on tour never received. The few remaining cards now face the toughest competition from them. McGinley noted that the real pain will be felt when these returning stars try to keep their status for the following year. The situation creates a brutal environment for players who did not leave the game for the breakaway league.

Rory McIlroy sees the return of DeChambeau as a positive step for the sport overall. The Northern Irishman believes the attention DeChambeau commands brings more eyes to the game. "I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy said, according to Yahoo Sports. While McGinley worries about the cards, McIlroy focuses on the boost in visibility for fans and sponsors.

Kinnings believes the plan will benefit the tour as a whole by ensuring top players remain visible for fans. The tour plans to launch its 2027 season next week with the BMW Australian PGA Championship.

DeChambeau quoted Arnold Palmer to make his point about humility. "Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," DeChambeau said, according to Yahoo Sports. This shift in tone was preceded by backlash over his conduct at The Open in July.

Dominating the DP World Tour to earn a PGA Tour card back for 2028 is his clear plan. Reaching this goal requires him to secure a top 10 finish in the Race to Dubai standings. DeChambeau's first step is the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa next month. His 2027 campaign is anticipated to launch with The Hero Dubai Desert Classic in January.

title: DP World Tour Offers Star Invites To LIV Defectors
article_text:
The professional golf world faces a new reality as the DP World Tour moves to fill its fields with high-profile names from the collapsing LIV Golf circuit. Nine players who left their original tours to join the Saudi-backed league have been offered a path back through sponsor invitations, a move that prioritizes star power over traditional meritocratic rankings. This shift comes as LIV Golf winds down through bankruptcy proceedings, leaving many players in limbo while tour officials scramble to stabilize the game's ecosystem.

According to Rediff, European Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings acknowledged the rapid shift in the sport, stating, "There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months." The tour is now offering these invitations without the hefty appearance fees that characterized the LIV era, aiming to inject excitement into lower-ranked events. This strategy targets specific stops that need a boost in star power, ensuring fields remain competitive even if depleted of top-tier members. According to Ronan MacNamara from Irish Golfer Magazine, up to 34 individuals previously associated with LIV are set to retain DP World Tour status in the coming year, a figure appearing inflated due to the former league's hostile maneuvers against the tour.

The tour has secured the returns of major stars like Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, and Bryson DeChambeau, which officials view as a positive step for the DP World Tour. CODE Sports reports that Cameron Smith has also been offered a career lifeline following the collapse of LIV Golf, though the terms come with specific conditions. Dustin Johnson, Bubba Watson, Cameron Smith, and Joaquin Niemann are among those receiving a "specific number" of tournament invitations to beef up events where they play. These players, who previously defected with a seemingly endless supply of Saudi cash, now face a different reality as that funding disappears. The arrangement allows these high-profile names to compete without taking spots from lower-ranked players who earned their way through the system. Kinnings emphasized the pragmatic nature of this approach, noting that the tour has always kept the best interests of its entire membership at the forefront of its mind.

Longtime supporters of the European tour have raised concerns about the implications of this policy. The tour previously sent 10 players to the PGA Tour annually, yet now it risks banning PGA Tour players with greater profiles than those it is losing. The idea behind the sponsor invitations is to place these stars in European tour stops that need help, giving those tournaments a boost without taking away spots from fields that were already depleted. This creates a unique situation where players who never contributed to the tour are now being welcomed back with open arms. The move promises to be exciting for European golf fans and head honchos at the Tour, but it leaves rank-and-file members questioning the fairness of the system.

As the DP World Tour integrates these former LIV players, the relationship with the PGA Tour remains a critical factor. With the PGA Tour's partnership with Europe ending next year, talks continue to alter and prolong the agreement. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp confirmed on Wednesday evening that discussions are productive, stating, "both entities have a mutual desire to extend and modify our partnership." The modification will likely include how many PGA Tour cards are offered to leading players in Europe, but it is most certain to be fewer than before. This reduction in card availability adds another layer of complexity to the integration of these high-profile returnees.

Kinnings believes the upcoming season will be highly competitive despite these changes. He noted that with the return of major champions and the inclusion of former LIV stars, "Our 2027 season is set to be one of the most keenly contested campaigns in our 55-year history." The inclusion of players like Rahm and DeChambeau adds significant weight to the tour's schedule. However, the financial stability of these players remains uncertain as the LIV league dissolves.

The next major development will be the finalization of the 2027 season schedule and the specific allocation of cards for European players. The PGA Tour and DP World Tour must resolve their partnership terms before the season begins. The outcome of these negotiations will determine how many European players can access the PGA Tour and how the remaining spots are distributed.
